data.title: Lentigo — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Lentigo** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. Define lentigo.**
- Small (usually <5 mm), well-circumscribed, uniformly brown to brown-black macule due to increased number of melanocytes along the basal layer with elongated pigmented rete ridges; does not darken with sun (unlike freckle)

**Q2. Discuss the various types of lentigines (PYQ).**
- Lentigo simplex: childhood onset, any site including mucosa, not sun-related
- Solar (actinic/senile) lentigo — 'age/liver spots': sun-exposed areas of older adults (dorsa of hands, face), larger, irregular; marker of photodamage; may evolve to reticulated seborrhoeic keratosis or lichen planus-like keratosis
- PUVA lentigines: stellate dark lentigines after PUVA — atypical melanocytes
- Ink-spot (reticulated black solar) lentigo: very dark, irregular, fair skin after sunburn
- Mucosal: labial melanotic macule, genital (penile/vulval) lentiginosis, oral
- Lentiginosis syndromes: Peutz–Jeghers (perioral/buccal lentigines + hamartomatous GI polyps — STK11; GI, breast, pancreatic cancer risk), LEOPARD/Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines (PTPN11 — Lentigines, ECG conduction defects, Ocular hypertelorism, Pulmonary stenosis, Abnormal genitalia, Retardation of growth, Deafness), Carney complex (LAMB/NAME — PRKAR1A; cardiac myxomas, endocrine tumours), Laugier–Hunziker (acquired oral and nail pigmentation, benign), Cowden/Bannayan–Riley–Ruvalcaba (penile lentigines — PTEN), centrofacial lentiginosis, partial unilateral lentiginosis, xeroderma pigmentosum

**Q3. Histopathology of solar lentigo.**
- Elongated club/bud-shaped rete ridges with basal hyperpigmentation, increased (not nested, non-atypical) melanocytes, solar elastosis

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Freckle, junctional naevus (nests on histology), lentigo maligna (irregular, enlarging, asymmetric follicular pigmentation on dermoscopy — biopsy), pigmented actinic keratosis, flat seborrhoeic keratosis, café-au-lait macule, pigmented BCC

**Q5. What are the warning signs for lentigo maligna?**
- Asymmetry, irregular borders, variegation, enlargement on face of elderly; dermoscopy — asymmetric pigmented follicular openings, rhomboidal structures, annular-granular pattern, grey dots — needs biopsy

**Q6. Management.**
- Photoprotection; topical hydroquinone, tretinoin, triple combination
- Cryotherapy, Q-switched (532 nm Nd:YAG, ruby, alexandrite) and picosecond lasers, IPL, chemical peels
- Evaluate syndromic lentiginosis (cardiac, GI, endocrine) when multiple/mucosal from childhood

## Quick spotter facts
- Perioral and buccal lentigines + GI polyps — Peutz–Jeghers
- LEOPARD syndrome — PTPN11
- Enlarging irregular facial pigment in elderly — rule out lentigo maligna

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Lentigines). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
